candidates.next_evidence: Track post-merger enterprise revenue, enterprise customer count, retention, cross-sell between Coursera and Udemy Business, AI-course enrollment cadence, integration costs, and whether the combined platform improves measurable workplace outcomes.

memory_update.text: COUR should now be treated as the combined Coursera-Udemy public vehicle after the May 11, 2026 closing, not as a standalone Coursera-only platform.
UDMY should generally be removed as a standalone active candidate after the merger closing; keep historical Udemy Business metrics as segment evidence for COUR integration work.

For enterprise workforce upskilling, the chokepoint appears to be shifting from raw course inventory to skills taxonomy, HRIS/workflow integration, trusted content, enterprise retention, and auditable outcomes.
WDAY and MSFT are second-order but strategically important because they control employee systems of record, skills graphs, workplace distribution, and AI productivity workflows.

Need a separate pass on private or non-US-listed learning infrastructure vendors such as Cornerstone, Degreed, 360Learning, Pluralsight, SAP SuccessFactors, and Absorb, because several important chokepoint assets may not map cleanly to US-listed pure plays.

node: Enterprise workforce upskilling and corporate e-learning platforms
summary: Expanded the universe around the enterprise workforce upskilling node with emphasis on scarce or constrained capabilities: enterprise distribution, HR/workflow integrations, skills taxonomy, trusted AI/compliance/technical content, and measurable learning-to-work outcomes. The best-fit public candidates are not only pure-play course platforms; the chokepoint increasingly sits in systems of record such as HRIS, skills graphs, workflow platforms, and enterprise knowledge/data layers that can connect learning to roles, performance, compliance, and productivity.
